prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation; automation covers bay control, station coordination, external interfaces; protection/primary equipment under approved designs. Layers (supervisory, bay execution, protection) separated; loss of one never silently substituted. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): sequencing, permissives/interlocks, timestamps; produces Bay Status Digest (used by Glasswing); bay status supports alarm assessment; requests Breaker Control Unit operations only if mode/permissives allow. North/South Bay Controllers: separate scopes, never substitute; block close when not ready; shared equipment needs explicit coordination. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): independent protection; produces Relay Diagnostic Note (used by Larkspur); indications reviewed against feeder status/protection operation. North Protection Panel: feeder protection equipment; indications used by operator. Transformer Protection Panel: transformer-only protection, local indication. Breaker Control Unit: authoritative interlocks, executes permitted commands. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): operator interface; retains alarm/event info after clearing; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip (operator records response/outstanding action). Station Gateway: brokers authorized control-room/bay traffic (protocol mappings, addressing, access control); produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): produces Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive; holdover on loss. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative time-ordered as-received evidence, audited access, retention, holds, backup. Engineering Workstation: revision-controlled config, authorized review (not operational assessment); produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal. Station DC System: control power; produces Battery Load Test Record. Actors: Control Room Operator: directs/suspends automation; switching requests to Keystone; acknowledges alarms only after review; cleared indication not proof of fix; breaker status discrepancy abnormal until understood; considers DC system; produces Clearance Handoff Memo for unresolved conditions; after handback verifies alarm/equipment/evidence consistency before closing. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): station plan; produces Isolation Boundary Card; confirms handback before evidence available for engineering review. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): settings review, investigation support. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): confirms identity/local conditions before operation; sends Breaker Inspection Tag. Substation Supervisor: escalation, priorities, exceptional switching. Requirements: sequences with hold/stop points; local precedence; remote commands checked; unique revisions; no copied-value approval; pre-deploy checks; work windows.

New part:
S173: It rejects malformed, stale, or unauthorized requests and records each rejection with enough context for operations review.
S174: Station Supervisory Control System presents available controls and indications to authorized operating personnel.
S175: Control Room Operator issues state-changing requests only through approved operating procedures and the configured supervisory interface.
S176: Bay Automation Controller validates each received request against local mode, interlocks, command authority, and equipment availability before issuing bay-level outputs.
S177: Breaker Control Unit applies accepted output commands at the breaker interface and returns the resulting position and circuit-health indications.
S178: Bay Automation Controller compares returned indications with the requested state and identifies incomplete or contradictory operation.
S179: Bay Automation Controller uses the inspection tag to associate the applicable equipment context with an authorized record.
S180: Station Gateway carries updated indications through the station interface using configured quality and timestamp attributes.
S181: Station Supervisory Control System displays indication quality and stale-data status so operators can distinguish a current value from a retained value.
S182: Sequence Event Archive retains time-tagged changes and control outcomes for event reconstruction and operational review.
S183: Satellite Time Receiver supplies the station time reference used to align event timestamps, subject to configured quality checks.
S184: Bay Automation Controller monitors communication health and places affected points in a defined degraded state when updates exceed configured age limits.
S185: Station Gateway reports link condition and protocol errors without converting a communication failure into an equipment-state change.
S186: Tandem evaluates electrical quantities against approved settings and issues protective trip outputs without relying on supervisory communications.
S187: North Protection Panel applies its assigned zone logic and maintains trip paths independently of supervisory network availability.
S188: Transformer Protection Panel applies its assigned protective logic and reports abnormal protection conditions through its configured interface.
S189: North Bay Controller maintains local bay control within the approved operating mode when supervisory communications are interrupted.
S190: South Bay Controller reports local mode and control availability through its configured bay interface.
S191: Engineering Workstation supports approved configuration review and does not serve as a routine source of operating commands.
S192: Maintenance Remote Terminal access is restricted to authorized maintenance sessions and is not used to bypass local interlocks.
S193: Station DC System supports control and protection functions through monitored station supply circuits, and supply loss is indicated as an abnormal station condition.
S194: Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection event records and verifies that approved settings remain consistent with coordination requirements.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
